firetemple.title: Hello, fire
firetemple.summary: Rising warped noise through the HDR tail. Exists to exercise the foundation end to end.

scorecard.fallback: A static image in the same palette, or a dark CSS gradient.
useCases: Smoke test for the shader pipeline, HDR tail, shell and shared WGSL library
A warm abstract backdrop; it glows, but nothing about it has the shape of a flame yet

firetemple.title: Advected noise
firetemple.summary: Ways to make noise look carried by rising gas instead of sliding past as one texture, side by side on the same heat field: scroll, domain warp, flow noise, curl displacement, a two-phase flow blend, and the combination that measures best.

scorecard.fallback: A looping video or animated WebP of the chosen variant; a still frame loses the whole point.
useCases: Choosing how a procedural flame, smoke or ember bed is animated: every variant is one call in advect.wgsl
Seeing what a moving-noise trick costs in noise evaluations before spending it per pixel
A warm abstract fire wall (the backdrop preset) where no flame shape is needed

firetemple.title: Blackbody colour
firetemple.summary: Temperature to colour three ways (Planck integral, polynomial fit, lookup texture) with their error, and a brightness mapping tamed enough to use.

scorecard.fallback: A static image of the chart; the colours themselves are available to CSS from the TypeScript twin.
useCases: Colouring a simulated temperature field: blackbody_radiance(t, t_ref, gamma) per pixel
Tinting lights, embers and sparks by temperature without a texture binding (blackbody_tint)
Choosing between the fit and the lookup texture: this scene shows the error of each

firetemple.title: Bloom tuned for fire
firetemple.summary: A chart of hot shapes at known radiance, to find how little bloom still reads as heat: threshold, knee, radius, levels, and half against full resolution.

scorecard.fallback: A still image of the chart; it is a tuning tool, not decoration.
useCases: Choosing bloom settings for an effect before spending GPU time on them
Checking that paper white does not glow and that thin, hot detail does
The scene the bloom cost study sweeps `levels` and resolution over

firetemple.title: Compositing over the page
firetemple.summary: One flame, smoke and logs written to a see-through canvas five ways: what an overlay effect has to put in alpha to read on a dark page and a light one.

scorecard.fallback: A transparent PNG or WebP of the flame with the same alpha, or nothing: it is decoration.
useCases: Reference for every overlay effect: copy the alpha mode and underlay that suit the page
Checking a theme: switch presets over the dark and the light page to see what survives
A small campfire or hearth decoration that sits on the page instead of in a box

firetemple.title: Fire as a light source
firetemple.summary: Wandering flames light a stone page and the cards on it: windowed inverse-square falloff, normal-mapped relief and analytic soft shadows from rounded rectangles.

scorecard.fallback: A static dark image with a warm radial-gradient glow and CSS drop shadows on the cards, offset away from the glow.
useCases: Fire, embers or a cursor torch that lights the DOM cards around it and throws their shadows across the page
Top-down 2D scenes: torches and camp fires lighting a normal-mapped floor
The lighting half of any flame effect: the falloff, shadow and tint functions are a shared chunk

firetemple.title: Flame colour ramps
firetemple.summary: One flame through eight colour ramps: blackbody, an authored fire gradient, a banded toon ramp, a blue gas flame and four chemical tints, each as a formula and as a baked texture.

scorecard.fallback: A static image; the same ramps are available to CSS gradients from the TypeScript twins.
useCases: Picking the heat-to-colour mapping for any procedural or simulated flame
Themed fire: copper green, sodium yellow, potassium lilac, lithium crimson, blue gas
Art-directed or banded gradients baked from colour stops into one small texture

firetemple.title: Flame shaping
firetemple.summary: One flame at three stages: a teardrop or taper distance field, the heat left after turbulence and erosion, and that heat through the fire ramp.

scorecard.fallback: A static image or a short looping video of the flame; the diagram panels can be a PNG.
useCases: Reference for the shared flame.wgsl chunk: every 2D flame effect starts from these functions
Tuning a silhouette (width, turbulence, erosion, falloff) before building a candle, torch or jet
A single stylised flame for a hero or a card, using the full-frame "flame" view

firetemple.title: Flicker signals
firetemple.summary: The shared flicker signal driving three candles, with a scrolling trace of each against the 10% band that defines a flash. Capped by default; the uncapped path is an explicit switch.

scorecard.fallback: The same signal from src/gpu/emission/flicker.ts driving a CSS opacity or filter on a still image; it is plain TypeScript and needs no GPU.
useCases: Intensity and position flicker for any flame, torch, ember bed or firelight on the site, safe by default
One signal shared by a WebGPU flame and the CSS glow around it, so the two stay in step
Checking a flicker setting against the flash threshold before it ships: the trace shows what the cap does to it

firetemple.title: Heat haze
firetemple.summary: Rising hot air bends what is behind it: a noise-driven refraction of a backdrop texture, masked by heat, with a faint colour fringe and softening where it is hottest.

scorecard.fallback: The backdrop itself, undistorted, with a still glow at its base. The haze is decoration: nothing is lost without it.
useCases: The air above any flame, ember bed, exhaust or hot surface in a scene the canvas draws itself
Shimmer over a hero image or a video frame uploaded as a texture
Not over live page content: a canvas cannot read the pixels of the DOM behind it

firetemple.title: Smoke shading
firetemple.summary: A ray-marched smoke plume lit from below by its fire and from above by a dim sky, comparing three ways to self-shadow it.

scorecard.fallback: A still frame of the plume as a transparent PNG; smoke moves slowly enough that a still reads as smoke.
useCases: Reference for shading smoke in the volumetric fire effects: soot colour, self-shadowing, underlight
A smoke column over a hero or a card, on a dark or a light page (it has real coverage)
Choosing a self-shadowing method by eye: switch `shadowing` between none, gradient and march

firetemple.title: Soft additive sprites
firetemple.summary: Embers, sparks and glow puffs as instanced additive quads: procedural shapes, velocity stretch, and the soft-particle depth fade that hides where a sprite cuts through geometry.

scorecard.fallback: A still frame of the scene; sprites alone can also be a CSS radial-gradient per ember on a dark backdrop.
useCases: Embers and sparks rising off any fire, drawn over a 3D scene or over a 2D flame
Glow halos and firelight in haze that must not show a seam where they meet walls and floors
The draw stage of a GPU particle system: the chunk and the renderer take any instance buffer
As drawn here it is an opaque dark scene; additive sprites on their own add nothing to a white page and need a dark region behind them

firetemple.title: Volume ray-march kernel
firetemple.summary: An emissive flame and absorbing smoke integrated in one ray march, at reduced resolution, upsampled under the depth buffer so edges against geometry stay sharp.

scorecard.fallback: A looped video or flipbook of the same shot; the march has no cheaper live equivalent.
useCases: The integration kernel under every volumetric fire and smoke effect on the site
A 3D fire that geometry can stand in front of, inside and behind
Choosing step count, march resolution, jitter and upsample filter for a volumetric effect

firetemple.title: Candle flame
firetemple.summary: One candle on the page: a teardrop flame with a blue foot, a dark wick and a soft halo over a wax body. It sways on its own and leans away from the pointer.

scorecard.fallback: The poster as a transparent image, or an inline SVG candle with a CSS animation on the flame path; with reduced motion the still frame is the whole effect.
useCases: A memorial, vigil or "lit" state: one calm flame beside a name, a date or a heading
A cursor toy on a landing page: the flame bends as the pointer passes and springs back
A row of tea lights as a quiet footer or loading state, one small canvas each

firetemple.title: Ember bed
firetemple.summary: A bed of glowing coals: dark crusts, cracks that breathe, and heat drifting slowly across it. The coal layout is baked once, so a frame is three texture fetches.

scorecard.fallback: The poster: a still of the bed reads the same, since nothing in it moves fast. A CSS radial gradient from dark red to black is the cheapest stand-in.
useCases: A calm, warm background for a hero, a footer or a card, safe to leave running
The base of a fire: put a flame effect above it, or sparks over it
A loading or idle state that should feel warm without drawing the eye
It is an opaque dark picture, so it works on a light page as an image does, in its own box

firetemple.title: Fire ring
firetemple.summary: A flame bent round a circle: tongues lick outward or inward from a ring, seamless all the way round, with a progress value that lights only part of it. Transparent in the middle.

scorecard.fallback: A still image of the ring, or a CSS conic-gradient ring with a blur; for the loader, the CSS ring with its own rotation.
useCases: A portal or a summoning circle with page content showing through the middle
A burning frame round an avatar or a badge
A loader or a progress ring: `progress` lights the arc from twelve o’clock clockwise

firetemple.title: Firelight background
firetemple.summary: The warm, slowly shifting light of a fire that is just out of frame. No flames: an opaque, calm backdrop for a dark page, steady enough to sit behind text.

scorecard.fallback: A CSS radial gradient in the same colours, which is most of the picture; or a still of the canvas.
useCases: An ambient backdrop behind an article or a hero on a dark page, under a veil and text
A warm fill behind a fire effect that is drawn on top of it
A login or landing screen that should feel lit by a hearth without showing one

firetemple.title: Fireplace
firetemple.summary: A whole hearth in one fragment pass: three layers of flame behind charred logs with glowing undersides, firelight on the wall and floor, and embers rising, with no simulation state.

scorecard.fallback: The poster, or a short looping video of the same scene; a still fireplace still reads as one.
useCases: A hero or a card that should feel like sitting by a fire
A cosy background for a landing page, a menu or a holiday banner
A "low evening fire" or "dying embers" idle state: the presets go down to a glow
It is an opaque scene with its own dark room, so a light page shows it as a picture in a box

firetemple.title: Flame strip
firetemple.summary: A band of flame tongues along the bottom edge of a wide, short canvas. It repeats exactly once per canvas width, so it tiles at any width, and is see-through above the flames.

scorecard.fallback: A horizontally repeating animated WebP or a short looping video of one period, anchored to the bottom edge; a still of it under reduced motion.
useCases: A section break: a short full-width band of flame between two blocks of content
The top edge of a footer, or the bottom edge of a hero, with the page showing above it
A low ember line under a heading or along the bottom of a card

firetemple.title: Gas jet
firetemple.summary: A blue directional flame: a tight cone with a pale inner cone, alone, in a row or as a stove burner seen from above, and with shock diamonds along it for an exhaust.

scorecard.fallback: The poster as a transparent image, or a CSS gradient cone (blue to transparent) with a blurred pale core; the jet barely moves, so a still loses little.
useCases: A burner or pilot light as a state: on, heating, cooking, boosting
Rocket, thruster and afterburner exhausts behind a logo, a ship or a launch button
A blowtorch or welding flame as a cursor trail tip or a progress indicator head

firetemple.title: Heat-haze overlay
firetemple.summary: Hot air on its own: an image or a video shimmering in a band, a plume or all over, with no flame in sight. Drop a photo or a video file on it to try your own.

scorecard.fallback: The image or the video itself, undistorted. The shimmer is decoration: nothing is lost without it.
useCases: A hero photograph of a road, a desert, a runway or a grill that should feel hot
The air above an exhaust, a chimney or an engine in a product shot or a video loop
Not over live page content: a canvas can only distort an image, a video or what it draws itself

firetemple.title: Scrolling-noise flame
firetemple.summary: The classic: noise scrolled upward, shaped by a height gradient, through a fire ramp. A wall of flame along the bottom edge, with five noise sources to compare.

scorecard.fallback: A looping video or animated WebP of the flame wall with the same alpha; a still poster under reduced motion.
useCases: A wall of fire along the bottom of a hero or a full-bleed section, over the page
A background for a dark landing page, with the flames kept below the headline
Starting point for any 2D flame: the gradient-minus-noise recipe in its smallest form

firetemple.title: Stateless sparks
firetemple.summary: Sparks that rise, wobble, cool and die with no buffers and no particle state: each pixel finds its spark from two hashes, in a few depth layers.

scorecard.fallback: Nothing, or a still transparent image of a few sparks: it is decoration and the page loses no meaning without it.
useCases: Embers drifting up behind a dark hero or over a fire drawn by another effect
A welding or grinding spray from a point: a button, a logo, a cursor
Dark pages only. Over a light page a spark is a few pale orange pixels and does not read
Any place a particle system would be overkill: it costs the same with ten sparks or a thousand
The welding spray and grinder presets are over the flash threshold when they fill a large view: keep them small

firetemple.title: Toon fire
firetemple.summary: Cartoon fire: three or four flat bands of colour with hard edges and an ink outline, redrawn ten times a second like a hand-animated cel. Opaque paint, so it sits on a light page.

scorecard.fallback: An SVG or a short sprite-sheet loop of the same flame: flat shapes are exactly what those formats are good at.
useCases: A campfire, torch or hazard marker in a game UI or an illustrated page
A flame icon or a streak badge that needs to read at 48 pixels and on a white background
Coloured "magic" fire (the spirit and toxic palettes) where realism would look out of place

firetemple.title: Torch and brazier
firetemple.summary: Up to 48 small flames in one canvas, each on a torch or in a brazier and each with its own seed, in a loop that closes exactly. Built to find out what many small flames cost.

scorecard.fallback: A sprite sheet or animated WebP baked from one loop of the effect (it repeats exactly), or the poster as a still.
useCases: List markers, bullets and status icons: many small flames drawn by one canvas laid over the list
A row of wall torches or braziers along a header, a sidebar or a section edge
A seamless loop to bake into a sprite sheet for places WebGPU does not reach

firetemple.title: Burn front on a fuel map
firetemple.summary: Burning paper: a sheet over the page that a tap or a stray ember lights. A thin glowing front crosses it, char follows and crumbles, the page shows through the hole, and the sheet grows back.

scorecard.fallback: A looping video with alpha of one burn, or a still of the half-burnt sheet; under reduced motion any frame is a complete picture.
useCases: A cover that burns away to reveal what is under it: a hero image, a spoiler, the next section
A page or route transition, lit from where the visitor clicked
A card or panel that burns when dismissed and leaves the page showing through

firetemple.title: Reaction–diffusion combustion
firetemple.summary: Fire as a travelling front in two continuous fields, temperature and fuel. Heat diffuses into unburnt fuel, the fuel ignites and releases heat; the speed and thickness of the front follow from the physical constants. Tap or drag to light it.

scorecard.fallback: A looping video of the fronts crossing with the same alpha, or the still poster; under reduced motion one frame is a complete picture of fronts and char.
useCases: A page or hero that burns: fronts creep over the content, leave char and the ground grows back
Touch-to-ignite surfaces where the fire has to spread at a believable, tunable speed
The reference model to compare a rule-based burn front against: speed, width and extinction come from constants

firetemple.title: DOM as fuel
firetemple.summary: The page is the fuel: the rounded rectangles of marked elements are drawn into a fuel map, so fire climbs cards and headings, stops at the gaps between them, leaves a scorch that fades, and the fuel returns.

scorecard.fallback: Nothing: it is decoration on top of real content, which is still there without it. A CSS box-shadow glow on hover is the nearest static stand-in.
useCases: A page that catches fire where it is clicked: a 404, a launch page, a game menu
Cards or headings that burn on a destructive action (delete, dismiss) and come back
Ambient embers smouldering on a dark landing page without hiding its content

firetemple.title: Doom fire
firetemple.summary: The PSX Doom heat automaton on a small grid of its own: a bottom row held hot, heat climbing one cell a step. Draw fire with a pointer, let it die and relight it, drive it from scroll or sound.

scorecard.fallback: A looping video or animated WebP of the wall of fire with the same alpha (the pointer drawing is lost); a still poster under reduced motion. The render-pass solver is plain enough to port to WebGL2.
useCases: A wall of fire along the bottom of a hero, a footer or a 404 page that visitors can draw into
Retro and pixel-art pages: the original palette and blocky cells are one preset away
A fire that answers the page: taller while the visitor scrolls, or in time with music

firetemple.title: Forest-fire automaton
firetemple.summary: A landscape that burns, regrows and burns again: the Drossel–Schwabl forest-fire automaton on a small grid, with wind, lightning and smoke. Tap or drag to start a fire.

scorecard.fallback: The poster: a still of the map with a fire on it. The rule is a few lines and runs on a 2D canvas at this grid size, so a CPU port is a realistic second step; a looped video cannot be touched.
useCases: A slow, living background for a hero or a section that rewards being left alone for a minute
An interactive piece: visitors start fires with a tap or a drag and watch where the wind takes them
Explaining self-organised criticality, fire regimes or wind-driven spread with something that runs
It is an opaque map, so it works on a light page as an image does, in its own box

firetemple.title: 3D combustion
firetemple.summary: Fuel, heat and smoke carried by a 3D stable-fluids solver, burning above an ignition temperature, and ray-marched as blackbody flame and fire-lit smoke over a small scene.

scorecard.fallback: A looped video or flipbook of the same shot (story 8.6), or the 2D grid fire of Epic 6 for a flat view.
useCases: A hero scene with a fire the camera can go round: campfire, brazier, gas burner
Fire that reacts to the scene: wind, a burst of fuel, a burner turned up
The upper bound of what a browser can simulate in 3D within a frame budget

firetemple.title: Fluid fire
firetemple.summary: Fire as a fluid: fuel, temperature and soot carried by an incompressible flow, burning above an ignition temperature, lifting by buoyancy and expanding where it burns. Burners, a torch you draw with (press and drag), wood, gas and chemical colours, and the three ways to keep a coarse grid lively side by side.

scorecard.fallback: There is no render-pass version of the solver, so no WebGL2 path: an Epic 4 shader fire (noise-flame, fireplace, gas-jet) or a looping video. Under reduced motion the first frame is already a burning fire.
useCases: A hero or backdrop fire that reacts to a visitor: drag to spray burning fuel, flames that bend round each other
Burners as page furniture: a strip along the footer, a ring round an avatar, a gas jet
The combustion layer later effects reuse (obstacles, heat haze over the page) and the reference for the cheaper fires

firetemple.title: Fire as page distortion
firetemple.summary: A hidden heat source below the frame sends a plume of hot gas up through a fluid simulation, and the gas bends the picture behind it: the shimmer rises, curls and fades with the gas instead of scrolling on its own. The pointer is a torch. Drop a photo or a video file on it to try your own.

scorecard.fallback: The picture itself, undistorted, or the noise-driven heat-haze overlay (no compute) for a shimmer that does not follow a flow.
useCases: A hero image above a grill, a radiator or an exhaust whose shimmer should rise and swirl like real hot air
A pointer that warms the page it passes over: text and images waver behind it and settle
Not over live page content: a canvas can only bend an image, a video or what it draws itself

firetemple.title: Fire round obstacles
firetemple.summary: Hot gas from a burner under the page rises through a fluid simulation and meets the page as solid walls: the marked cards, headings and buttons. The plume splits round them, curls over their top edges and leaves smoke pooled under overhangs. Press to add heat.

scorecard.fallback: Nothing: it is decoration round real content, which is still there without it. The still poster, or a CSS glow under the cards, is the nearest stand-in.
useCases: A landing page or a 404 whose cards and headings sit in a rising fire and shape it
Showing that a simulation knows where the page is: flow that parts round elements and pools under them
Judging the solver against solids: the SDF test shapes (card row, circle, slanted plate) without a page

firetemple.title: Stable fluids
firetemple.summary: The validation scene of the grid-fluid solver ported from Water Temple: smoke and ember glow rising from a smouldering bed, carried by an incompressible velocity field on a staggered grid. Drag to stir it; the controls switch the advection scheme, the pressure solver, vorticity confinement and the grid size.

scorecard.fallback: There is no render-pass version of the solver, so no WebGL2 path: the still poster, or a looping video of the plume. Under reduced motion the first frame is already a plume.
useCases: Checking the solver every Epic 6 effect builds on: schemes, solvers and confinement side by side
Smoke that a visitor can stir, over a dark or a light page
The starting point for combustion: temperature, fuel and smoke in the dye, buoyancy and expansion built in

firetemple.title: Embers
firetemple.summary: Flying embers as real particles: they rise off a hidden fire line, drift in curl-noise air, cool along the blackbody curve from yellow-orange to deep red and out, and twinkle each at its own pace. Press and drag to wave a torch through them.

scorecard.fallback: The stateless `sparks` effect (a fragment shader, no compute) in its campfire preset, or nothing: embers are decoration and the page loses no meaning without them.
useCases: Embers drifting up over a dark hero, a footer or the whole page, behind or in front of the content
Over a fire drawn by another effect: the particles carry the heat above the flames
A torch that follows a press and drag, leaving a trail of embers that drift off on the air
Scroll or music driven: the drive adds embers as a share of the calm rate, never speed
Dark pages only: on a light page an ember is a few pale orange pixels

firetemple.title: Directed jet
firetemple.summary: A flamethrower or dragon breath: a nozzle drives fuel, heat and momentum into the 2D fire fluid, and burning droplets, flame sprites and embers ride its velocity field, spreading, curling into eddies and rising as the jet slows, under the smoke the fluid makes. The nozzle aims at the pointer.

scorecard.fallback: The `gas-jet` shader (a directional flame with no simulation) for the burning cone, or a looping video; a still poster under reduced motion.
useCases: A showpiece hero: a flamethrower that follows the pointer, or a dragon breathing across a section
A jet splashing against a page element (the wall preset): flame rolling along a surface
Any particles that should be carried by a simulated flow rather than by noise

firetemple.title: Fireworks
firetemple.summary: Aerial shells as multi-stage emitters, entirely on the GPU: a shell rises with a spark tail and breaks at its apogee into a peony, chrysanthemum, willow, ring, palm, crossette, crackle or glitter burst, in the colours of real emitter salts. Click or tap to send one up to the pointer.

scorecard.fallback: A still poster of a burst, or nothing: fireworks are celebration, not content. There is no fragment-only version; a few shells as CPU sprites (`soft-sprites`) would be the cheapest stand-in.
useCases: A celebration over a dark hero, a launch page or a "thank you" screen, with shells going up on their own
A click or tap that answers with a shell bursting where the pointer is
Scroll or music driven: the drive adds shells to the schedule, never speed
Over a page as an overlay: on a dark page the bursts are light; on a light page they are confetti

firetemple.title: Sorting and blending
firetemple.summary: Fire and smoke puffs drawn four ways: all additive, alpha in buffer order, alpha after a GPU depth sort, and weighted blended order-independent transparency, side by side.

scorecard.fallback: A still frame as a transparent PNG; smoke and a small fire read as a still. A study scene, not something to ship.
useCases: Choosing how to blend smoke particles: the sort and OIT modules plug into any particle buffer
Seeing where each method fails: glowing smoke, wrong occlusion, popping, OIT colour bias
A fire with a smoke column over a dark or a light page: the smoke has real coverage

firetemple.title: Particle flame
firetemple.summary: The original particle-system fire: large soft sprites born hot at a base, lifted by their own heat, pulled into a taper, licked about by curl noise, cooling and shrinking until they overlap into a flame body, with embers thrown off the tips. Press to light a fire where you press.

scorecard.fallback: The `noise-flame` wall (one fragment pass, no compute) or the `candle` and `torch` shader flames; a still poster under reduced motion.
useCases: A campfire, torch or candle that responds to wind and to the pointer, over a dark hero or a card
A fire lit where the visitor presses and dying down when they let go
Several small flames in one canvas: the cost follows the sprites drawn, not the canvas area
The building block for a scene that also wants embers and sparks from the same particle pool

firetemple.title: GPU particle system
firetemple.summary: The Epic 7 particle framework laid bare: a pool of up to a million particles born, moved, collided and recycled entirely on the GPU, with every emitter shape, force and collider switchable and the live count in the HUD.

scorecard.fallback: None needed: it is a test scene for the framework, not page decoration. The effects built on the framework name their own fallbacks.
useCases: Checking what the framework does before building on it: shapes, rates, bursts, forces, colliders, GPU spawning, the external velocity field
The scene the particle scale study (7.10) sweeps: `count` sets the pool from 1 024 to 1 048 576 and the emission keeps it about `fill` full
A reference for the 2D overlay space (canvas heights) and the 3D scene space side by side

firetemple.title: Particle trails
firetemple.summary: Two ways to give a particle a trail, side by side on the same particles: ribbons built from each particle’s own history of positions, and an HDR buffer that fades a little every frame. Comets, a sparkler and embers in a vortex; press to throw sparks.

scorecard.fallback: Velocity-stretched sprites (the sprite renderer’s `stretch` and `trail`) give a short comet tail with no history at all; without WebGPU, the stateless `sparks` effect.
useCases: Comets, meteors and thrown sparks whose path should stay visible behind them
A sparkler or a pointer trail: short bright streaks that follow the motion
Embers caught in a vortex, where the trail shows the flow
Choosing between ribbons and an accumulation buffer for a particle effect of your own

firetemple.title: Spark shower
firetemple.summary: A grinder, welding or forge shower of sparks as GPU particles: white-hot streaks arc under gravity and drag, cool along the blackbody curve, bounce off the floor, an anvil and the page’s own cards, and split on impact into smaller, cooler sparks. Move the pointer to aim the grinder; press to bite harder.

scorecard.fallback: The stateless `sparks` effect (a fragment shader, no compute) in its grinder preset kept small, or nothing: a spark shower is decoration and the page loses no meaning without it.
useCases: A grinder or welding spray from a point on a dark page: a hero, a product shot, a cursor
Sparks that land on the page’s own cards and buttons, skid off their edges and split
A forge with an anvil and hammer strikes, as a section header or a loading moment
Scroll or music driven: the drive adds sparks as a share of the calm rate, never speed
Dark pages only: on a light page a spark is a thin pale streak

firetemple.title: Sparkler
firetemple.summary: A hand-held sparkler as GPU particles: a white-hot core throws thousands of tiny sparks a second that live a fraction of a second and fork mid-flight into two or three, the branching look. The pointer is the hand; left alone, the tip traces a slow figure of eight and leaves an afterimage.

scorecard.fallback: A small looping video or a still image of a sparkler, or nothing: it is decoration and the page loses no meaning without it.
useCases: A celebration moment on a dark page: a launch, a birthday, a new year
A cursor that writes in light: the sparkler follows the pointer and leaves an afterimage
A dark hero or card that is never still: left alone, the tip traces a slow figure of eight
Scroll or music driven: the drive adds sparks as a share of the calm rate, never speed
Dark pages only: on a light page the sparks are thin pale lines

watertemple.title: Hello, water
watertemple.summary: Domain-warped noise. Exists to exercise the foundation end to end.

scorecard.fallback: A static image in the same palette, or a plain CSS background colour.
useCases: Smoke test for the shader pipeline, shell and shared WGSL library
A quiet abstract backdrop; nothing about it reads as water yet

watertemple.title: Wave-crest subsurface scattering
watertemple.summary: Big, backlit waves where the tall, thin crests glow green-blue as the sun shines through them. One view- and light-dependent term; proves sss.wgsl.

scorecard.fallback: A still render of backlit swell with the glow baked in; the term is view dependent but a single frame reads fine as a poster.
useCases: The translucent glow on wave crests in an ocean shader (feeds the ocean shading story)
Backlit water, waterfalls and sheets of liquid that need a cheap "light through it" cue

watertemple.title: Depth absorption

watertemple.title: Ripples around page elements
watertemple.summary: Water behind a real page where the page itself is solid: elements marked data-wt-obstacle are measured every frame and become walls of the wave solver, so ripples bend around a card, bounce off a headline and are pushed by a card that moves.

watertemple.title: Ink in a tank (3D fluid)
watertemple.summary: A drop of ink released in a glass tank of water sinks, rolls up into a vortex ring and breaks into tendrils. A volumetric stable-fluids solve (48 to 96 cells, multigrid pressure, vorticity confinement, MacCormack ink) in compute shaders, drawn by a ray march with coloured absorption and a precomputed light volume. Tap to release a drop, drag to push the water, drag the background to orbit.

scorecard.fallback: Without WebGPU, or without compute shaders, show a looping video or animated WebP of the same ink in water on a CSS background (the idle autonomous strokes loop well), with a plain CSS gradient behind it; the interaction is the part that does not survive, so keep the page working without it.

watertemple.summary: Luminous RGB trails in a stable fluid on a dark background, with heads smoothly cycling through red, green and blue together while their tails keep the colours they were laid with. watertemple.summary: Water that actually flows: a shallow-water solver on the GPU moves a depth and a velocity over terrain. A dam breaks and the surge rushes around pillars, a spring runs down a hillside into a lake, a tide fills and drains rock pools. Pour water, push it, dig channels.

watertemple.title: Screen-space fluid surface
watertemple.summary: A cloud of particles turned into a continuous, refracting liquid: sphere impostors, depth smoothing (bilateral against narrow-range), thickness, normals and a composite with absorption, reflection and a sun highlight. Three synthetic sources (a ball that splits and merges, a wave, a pouring stream) stand in for a solver; one control swaps between the finished surface, the bag of marbles it replaces and each intermediate image.

scorecard.fallback: A looping video or poster of the liquid. There is no useful cut-down without WebGPU: the particles come from a compute solver, so a WebGL2 version would be a different effect (a metaball SDF blob, see Epic 9).
useCases: A dedicated showpiece page where a pouring, sloshing or splashing liquid is the product (a drink, a pool toy, a tank game)
The renderer behind any particle solver in Epic 7: SPH, position-based fluids or MLS-MPM hand over positions and get a liquid
Not a background or a card: on a laptop it needs the whole GPU budget of a Tier C page

watertemple.title: MLS-MPM water tank
watertemple.summary: A tank of water simulated with the moving-least-squares material point method: 100 000 particles carry the fluid, a background grid does the physics, and there is no neighbour search. A wall pushes in and out and sends waves down the tank to break on a beach; or let a dam burst around pillars, or pour a stream into a pool. Drag through the water to push it, tap to drop a blob, drag empty space to orbit. Drawn as a refracting liquid by the screen-space fluid surface, or as the spheres, speed or density it is made of.

scorecard.fallback: A looping video or poster of the tank. Nothing cheaper reproduces it: the fluid needs compute shaders and atomics, so a WebGL2 version would be a different effect (a shallow-water heightfield, see the shallow-water effect, or a ray-marched blob, Epic 9).
useCases: A dedicated showpiece page where a body of water sloshing, breaking and splashing is the product: a tank game, a drink, a water toy, a landing experience
The reference for a particle fluid with no neighbour search, at counts the neighbour-search solvers (SPH, position-based fluids) cannot reach
Not a background or a card, and not for phones: it needs a discrete or Apple Silicon GPU and most of a Tier C frame budget

watertemple.title: Particle field and neighbour grid
watertemple.summary: A fountain of up to a million spray particles carried by a curl-noise flow, drawn as instanced billboards. The foundation of the particle fluids: a GPU particle system, a fixed-step integrator, and a uniform-grid neighbour search built by a counting sort and prefix sum every frame. Colour the cloud by its neighbour counts, or light up the neighbours of the particle under the pointer, to see the search at work. Move the pointer to aim the nozzle, drag to orbit.

scorecard.fallback: Without WebGPU or compute, show a looping video of the fountain, or a WebGL2 version that moves a few tens of thousands of particles with transform feedback or a vertex-shader flow; the neighbour views have no fallback and are a research tool, not a feature.
useCases: Mist, spray, snow, embers and dust that need hundreds of thousands of GPU-simulated sprites: the cheapest honest particle effect, and the framework the fluid solvers build on
A hero or landing-page set piece where the particles are the subject, on desktop-class GPUs
The reference for a GPU neighbour search (cell ids, counting sort, prefix sum, reorder) that SPH, position-based fluids and collisions reuse

watertemple.title: 2D position-based fluids
watertemple.summary: A tank of water as particles solved with position-based fluids (Macklin and Mueller): incompressibility is a constraint on positions, relaxed by a few parallel iterations per sub-step, so a big time step cannot blow the water up. A dam break that collapses and sloshes, a stream pouring onto a shelf, a wave-maker, drops falling into a calm pool. Drag to push the water, tap to drop a blob. Colour the particles by speed, by density error (how well the constraint holds) or by neighbour count; change the particle spacing and the same parameters give the same water.

scorecard.fallback: Without WebGPU or compute, show a looping video of the same scene (the dam break and the pour loop cleanly), or a heightfield water surface (Epic 4) if the point is only a sloshing top surface; the particle solver has no fragment-shader equivalent.
useCases: A hero or set piece where a body of water sloshes, splashes and can be pushed around, on desktop-class GPUs at around ten thousand particles
A loading or empty-state illustration: a stream filling a vessel, or drops falling into a pool
The 2D stepping stone to the 3D position-based fluids: the same solver, the same parameters, a quarter of the particles per unit of detail

watertemple.title: Position-based fluid tank (3D)
watertemple.summary: Water as ten thousand particles by default in a glass tank, solved with position-based fluids (Macklin and Mueller 2013) on the GPU and drawn as a refracting liquid surface. Three restartable scenes: a dam break with two pillars, a pour that fills the tank, and a wave tank with an oscillating wall. Drag empty space to orbit, drag through the water to push it, tap to drop a blob. Secondary spray, foam and bubbles follow the live water. Choose container mode to drag or shake the vessel, or enable device tilt. The particle count, solver iterations and sub-steps, viscosity, vorticity and the renderer quality are live.

scorecard.fallback: A captured poster of the tank (orbit, push and tilt are lost). There is no cheaper live version: a heightfield water surface (the 3D pool effect) loses the splashes, and a WebGL2 particle solver would need transform feedback and no neighbour search.
useCases: A dedicated landing page or product experience where pouring, sloshing and splashing water is the subject, on a desktop-class GPU
A game or toy where the player pushes real water around inside a container (drag, tilt, shake and wave-maker)
The reference for the stable, large-time-step particle fluid: the solver, the neighbour grid and the screen-space renderer working together

watertemple.title: 2D SPH liquid
watertemple.summary: A tank of water as thousands of particles: weakly compressible smoothed-particle hydrodynamics in compute shaders, drawn as one liquid body (soft blobs, a threshold, a rim, a highlight, refraction) instead of discs. A dam break that collapses and sloshes back, a stream pouring onto a shelf and an obstacle, two zero-gravity blobs that merge under surface tension. Drag to push the water, tap to drop a block of it.

scorecard.fallback: Without WebGPU or compute, show a looping video of the same scene (the dam break and the pour loop cleanly), or a WebGL2 version of the drawing over a few thousand particles stepped on the CPU; the simulation has no fragment-shader equivalent.
useCases: A hero or set piece where a body of water sloshes, splashes and can be pushed around, on desktop-class GPUs at around ten thousand particles
A loading or empty-state illustration: a stream filling a vessel, or a droplet that merges with another
The reference for particle-based liquid in 2D: the same solver and renderer serve the position-based-fluids comparison

hologpu.title: Quiet bokeh dust drift
hologpu.summary: A local T3 overlay of 256–2048 Gaussian dust quads. The default is 512 records, 4 CSS-pixel nominal diameter and 0.18 intensity, with warm ember, pearl and rose presets. Its default resolution scale is 0.5: the bilinear upscale softly blends the small Gaussian sprites while reducing the draw and resolve area. Explicit resolutionScale: 1 remains available. Effective DPR retains every geometry and interaction measurement in CSS pixels at either scale. --hgpu-tint and --hgpu-intensity drive the brand appearance. Dust has no meaning; keep the native page content in the light DOM.

hologpu.title: Quiet CSS-pixel dot matrix
hologpu.summary: A transparent technical backdrop with a regular CSS-pixel lattice. The default 24 px pitch and 1.15 px dot radius stay constant at DPR 1 and 2 and when resolution scale changes: the shader divides target resolution by the effective frame DPR. A signed-distance circle uses an analytic half-pixel edge. The shared value-noise chunk gently modulates radius and opacity by at most ±15%.

hologpu.title: Quiet film grain
hologpu.summary: A transparent T1 layer adds fine seeded film grain over an existing light or dark page background. Use attach(host, grain, { layer: 'front' }); light DOM content remains interactive. Default opacity is 4%. The image input is optional and only weights grain by image luminance; it does not paint the image itself.

hologpu.title: Quiet linked constellation
hologpu.summary: A transparent, faint network for a launch-page section. Each seeded grid cell holds one point and connects only to its eight immediate neighbours. The 88 CSS-pixel default pitch, 1.5 px point radius and 0.7 px stroke remain stable across DPR and resolution scale. Shorter connections fade in more strongly; linkDistance is expressed in lattice pitches. The default 0.22 point opacity and relative 0.28 connection opacity keep copy dominant.

hologpu.title: Quiet topographic contours
hologpu.summary: One T1 fragment pass evaluates a two-octave value-noise height field and draws isolines with fract and derivative antialiasing. Both stroke edges are integrated over a derivative pixel footprint, so subpixel lines fade with their coverage rather than keeping full brightness. Height amplitude is limited to 0.2 times the terrain wavelength: the bounded value-noise slope stays below one, so the height interval also supplies a lower bound on adjacent-line separation. spacing is clamped to at least 12 CSS pixels to control moiré. No textures, feedback, or optional WebGPU features are required.

hologpu.summary: How does neighbourhood cost change between edge extraction and painterly smoothing?

hologpu.title: Soft aurora veil
hologpu.summary: One T1 fragment pass uses two-octave value-noise fBm from the shared noise chunk, warped by two additional noise channels. The field bends three wide, softly overlapping bands. Colour stops interpolate in OKLCH with chroma-weighted circular hue; a flat base keeps contrast low. Static display-code-value dither reduces SDR banding. There are no optional WebGPU features or persistent simulation resources.

hologpu.title: Soft coloured card contact shadow
hologpu.summary: A T1 Gaussian contact shadow outside a rounded card. The default tint is blue-grey at 0.2 intensity. elevation is a CSS-driven 0…1 value: it spreads the shadow and moves its centre down by 3…15 CSS pixels. There is no time-driven motion; reduced motion keeps the same finished pose. Unchanged frames submit no GPU work.

hologpu.title: Soft perspective floor grid
hologpu.summary: A transparent, low-alpha perspective floor. Rays from a fixed camera intersect a horizontal plane. The plane coordinates form a regular grid, with line coverage derived from fwidth so the projected line weight is expressed in CSS pixels. High-frequency lines fade before they become unresolved; exponential distance fog and a soft horizon gate prevent a bright or shimmering vanishing point. Derivatives execute uniformly across the fragment pass.

hologpu.title: Soft press wavefront
hologpu.summary: A T1 circular wavefront after a button or card press. Four oldest-first event slots store normalized canvas position, start time and an active flag in one 64-byte uniform buffer, with a separate 16-byte interaction-clock uniform. A fifth press replaces the oldest slot. Every wave expires after 600 ms; initial and settled frames are transparent. There is no simulation or feedback texture. Idle fields do not submit GPU work.

hologpu.title: Soft specular light sweep
hologpu.summary: A single T1 fullscreen fragment pass evaluates an angled Gaussian band. The default intensity is 0.22; tint and intensity accept CSS tokens. Output is premultiplied linear colour, so attach it front over the real hero or image. The effect carries no information and leaves the underlying page visible.

hologpu.title: Sphere-traced sculpture

hologpu.title: Subtle product image depth parallax
hologpu.summary: This baseline T4 filter shifts a product image using an aligned, authored grayscale depth map. White represents near content and black leaves far content fixed. The effect owns no simulation or history: pointer, progress and image/depth changes drive one fragment pass, which settles between changes. The default amount is 0.015 of the displayed image width with intensity 0.25, giving at most 0.375% of width (2.25 CSS px on a 600 px image). Increasing intensity strengthens this motion, with an absolute vector displacement limit of 2% of image width even in combined mode. Reduced motion returns the original image with zero offset; amount or intensity 0 also preserves the image.
